title: Design Tokens & Variables
description: Learn how to build a systematic color palette using CSS custom properties and Figma variables. Start with hardcoded values and progressively refactor into a flexible, themeable token system.

steps.title: Define your base colors
steps.instruction: Start by choosing a primary color that represents your brand. We'll use a vibrant blue as our foundation and build the rest of the palette from there. Hardcoded hex values are the simplest starting point.
steps.code: .card { background: #3b82f6; color: #ffffff; border: 1px solid #e2e5eb; }

steps.title: Convert to CSS custom properties
steps.instruction: Now refactor those hardcoded values into CSS custom properties. This makes them reusable across your entire stylesheet. Define them on :root so they're available everywhere.
steps.code: :root { --color-primary: #3b82f6; --color-secondary: #06b6d4; --color-accent: #f59e0b; } .card { background: var(--color-primary); }

steps.title: Add semantic token names
steps.instruction: Go beyond raw colors and create semantic tokens. Instead of --color-blue, use --color-surface, --color-text, --color-border. This decouples your design from specific color values.
steps.code: :root { /* Semantic tokens */ --color-surface: #ffffff; --color-text: #121726; --color-border: #e2e5eb; }

steps.title: Enable theme switching
steps.instruction: The magic moment! Use data attributes to create theme variants. When you change [data-theme], all your variables update simultaneously. Every component using tokens adapts instantly.
steps.preview: One click, everything changes!

steps.title: Build gradient from tokens
steps.instruction: For the grand finale, derive a gradient from your token values. Now when the theme switches, even your gradients transform automatically. This is the power of a token-based system.
steps.preview: Gradient adapts to any theme!
